edition.name: Migne, Patrologia Latina 5 (1844), Arnobius, Disputationes adversus gentes, Liber I, via Latin Wikisource (Corpus Corporum TEI)
edition.witness_note: Single locked witness in repo; second witness not yet locked.

source_text: Quae sunt ista, inquies, clausa atque obscura mysteria, quae nulli nec homines scire, nec ipsi, qui appellantur, dii mundi, parte queunt aliqua suspicionis atque opinationis attingere, nisi quos ipse dignatus est cognitionis tantae impertire muneribus, et in abditos recessus thesauri interioris inducere. Vides enim, si nollet inferri sibi a quoquam manus, summa illi fuisse contentione nitendum, ut hostes ab se suos, vel potestate inversa prohiberet? Qui caecis restituerat lumina, is efficere si deberet, non poterat caecos? qui debilibus integritatem, is debiles reddere difficultati habuit, aut labori? qui claudos faciebat incedere, is motus alligare membrorum nervorum duritia nesciebat? qui extrahebat a tumulis mortuos, huic arduum fuerat letum cui vellet indicere? Sed quia fieri ratio ea, quae fuerant destinata, poscebat: et hic in ipso mundo, nec modo quam gestum est alio, inaestimabilis illa atque incredibilis lenitas injurias in se hominum, puerilibus pro ineptiis ducens, manus in se porrigi ab immanibus passa est, durissimisque latronibus, nec reputandum putavit, quid illorum dissignasset audacia, dummodo suis ostenderet, quid ab sese expectare deberent. Cum enim de animarum periculis multa, mala de illarum contra insinuator, magister atque auctor, ad officiorum convenientium fines, suas leges et constituta direxit: non superbiae factum comminuit? non libidinum extinxit flammas? non hiatum compressit aviditatis? non tela extorsit e manibus, atque omnia seminaria totius vitiositatis abscidit? Ipse denique non lenis, non placidus, non accessu facilis, non familiaris affatu, non humanas miserias indolescens, omnes omnino crucibus et corporalibus affectos malis unica illa benignitate miseratus, reddidit et restituit sanitati?
pass_a_gloss: What are these, you ask, closed and obscure mysteries, which neither men nor those who are called gods of the world can know, nor can they touch with any suspicion or opinion, except those to whom He Himself has deigned to impart the gifts of such great knowledge and lead into the hidden recesses of the inner treasure. For you see, if He did not want anyone to lay hands on Him, He would have had to strive with the greatest effort to prevent His enemies from doing so, or to prevent them by reversed power. He who restored sight to the blind, could He not make the blind if He had to? He who gave integrity to the weak, did He have difficulty making the weak or laboring? He who made the lame walk, did He not know how to bind the movements of limbs with hardness of nerves? He who raised the dead from their tombs, would it have been hard for Him to indicate death to whom He wished? But because reason demanded that what had been destined should happen, and He in this very world, not only as it was done elsewhere, endured that inestimable and incredible gentleness, the injuries of men against Him, considering them childish foolishness, allowed hands to be laid on Him by savage men and very harsh robbers, and did not think it worth considering what audacity they had assigned to themselves, as long as He showed His own what they ought to expect from Him. For when He, the insinuator, teacher, and author of many dangers to souls, directed His laws and established rules to the limits of suitable duties, did He not diminish the deed of pride? Did He not extinguish the flames of lust? Did He not compress the void of greed? Did He not wrench the weapons from their hands and cut off all the seedbeds of total vice? He Himself, finally, not gentle, not placid, not easily accessible, not familiar in speech, not unaware of human miseries, pitied all those afflicted with crosses and bodily evils with that unique benignity, restored and gave back to health?

choices.why: accurate translation of the Latin phrase
preserves the superlative sense of the Latin

rejected: And finally, He was not gentle
choices.why: maintains the contrast with the previous description of God's gentleness

pass_b_english: You ask what these closed and obscure mysteries are. Neither human beings nor those who are called gods of the world can know them, nor can they even touch them with any suspicion or opinion — except those to whom He Himself has deigned to impart the gifts of such great knowledge and to lead into the hidden recesses of the inner treasure.

You see, if He had not wanted anyone to lay hands on Him, He would have had to strive with the greatest effort to keep His enemies from doing so, or to prevent them by a reversal of power. The One who restored sight to the blind — could He not have made them blind if He had to? The One who gave wholeness to the weak — did He have any difficulty making them weak? The One who made the lame walk — did He not know how to bind the movements of limbs with the hardening of nerves? The One who drew the dead from their tombs — would it have been hard for Him to decree death for whomever He wished? But reason demanded that what had been destined should happen, and so, in this very world, not merely as it was done elsewhere, He endured the injuries of men against Him with an inestimable and incredible gentleness, treating them as childish foolishness. He allowed hands to be laid on Him by savage men and very harsh robbers, and He did not think it worth considering what audacity they had assigned to themselves, as long as He showed His own what they ought to expect from Him.

For when He — the insinuator, teacher, and author of many dangers to souls — directed His laws and established rules to the limits of suitable duties, did He not diminish the deed of pride? Did He not extinguish the flames of lust? Did He not compress the void of greed? Did He not wrench the weapons from their hands and cut off all the seedbeds of total vice? Finally, He Himself — not gentle, not placid, not easily approached, not familiar in speech, not unaware of human miseries — pitied all those afflicted with crosses and bodily evils with that unique benignity, and He restored them and gave them back to health.
